title: Checking Assumptions vs. Reality
text: Hi, I'm Bhavana, a Humanitarian's AI Fellow. Week 10 of my Job Seeker report, the job search app where I run SEO, making Google find and rank our listings. This week, nothing new got built. It's a checking week. Verify what actually works and honestly defer what isn't ready. Two things this week and only two. A full audit, confirm every acceptance criterion, then run

title: The Full Audit: Checking the Specs
text: Lighthouse. That branch ended at 100 out of 100 across every page tested. And a company page attempt, which ended somewhere more honest, scoped out for now to revisit once the real data exists. One win, one deliberate not yet. First, the audit. The spec has a real acceptance checklist and the discipline is boring but essential. Go through it

title: Lighthouse: Achieving a 100/100 SEO Score
text: One item at a time and confirm actual status, not the status you assume. JSON-LD on every job page, noindex on inactive ones, the sitemap index, the robots rules, canonical URLs, the indexing API. Each one checked against the running site, not against memory. Then the independent check. A self-assessment is easy to fool. So, the audit ran Lighthouse, Google's own tool,

title: Scoping Honestly: The Company Page Decision
text: Against the three kinds of page that matter. A job page, the landing templates, and the master directory. The result was the same every time. 100 out of 100 on SEO. Not my opinion of the work, a score anyone can reproduce. The other half was scoping honestly. Company detail pages were on the list, the same meta and canonical treatment job pages get. But a meta tag needs a real page with real content behind it. And the sponsorship data that would make one

title: Recap: Ship it or Scope it, Don't Fake it
text: Substantive isn't in place yet. So, rather than ship a thin page to check a box, the page noindexes itself until it's actually worth showing. Documented, deferred, not faked. The recap, checking not adding. The acceptance criteria confirmed one at a time against the running site. Lighthouse, 100 out of 100 on every page tested, a result anyone can reproduce. And the company page scoped out honestly instead of shipped thin because a meta tag with no real content behind it is just a box checked. The rule this week, ship it or scope it, but don't fake it. Your turn. Take a feature you've marked done and ask Claude for the difference between assumed status and real status. What would an independent tool actually report? Then find the item you're tempted to check off cheaply and ask whether it's genuinely shippable or whether the honest move is to scope it out until the data exists. Run this and audit your own done. Ship it or scope it.
